subject.title: [Feature]: Show session and requester context in macOS exec approval popup

question: What requester identity may the macOS approval popup disclose: the existing raw session key only, sanitized channel/sender/thread labels, or neither?
rationale: The code can mechanically render the existing field, but session keys and turn-source metadata may expose user, account, or conversation identifiers; repository behavior does not define the native popup's disclosure and redaction contract.

options.title: Sanitized Context
options.body: Introduce display-safe session, channel, sender, and thread labels with explicit omission, redaction, and truncation rules while retaining raw identifiers only for routing.

options.title: Session Key Only
options.body: Render the existing non-empty session key for parity with other approval surfaces and defer richer requester fields.

options.title: Keep Current Popup
options.body: Leave requester identity out of the native popup and rely on command, agent, host, and other existing details.

recommendation.title: Sanitized Context
recommendation.body: Introduce display-safe session, channel, sender, and thread labels with explicit omission, redaction, and truncation rules while retaining raw identifiers only for routing.

likelyOwner.reason: This person supplied the prior item-specific review and has adjacent macOS application history, making them the strongest available routing candidate for the native disclosure decision.
